slides.say: For every two numbers x and y that are not zero, diamond of x, y is x minus y, squared, over x times y cubed. Given: a and b are two different numbers, and neither of them is zero. Diamond of a, b over diamond of b, a is equal to what?

slides: The same two letters go into the diamond on the top and at the bottom, only in a different order. [short pause] We'll solve it three ways, the full math, reading the definition first, and plugging in numbers.

slides.say: [short pause] The top is diamond of a, b, so x is a and y is b. That's a minus b, squared, over a times b cubed. The bottom is diamond of b, a, so now x is b and y is a. That's b minus a, squared, over b times a cubed.
at: The top is diamond of a, b
The bottom is diamond of b, a

slides.say: To divide by a fraction, we multiply by its reciprocal. So we flip the bottom fraction and multiply. And a tip, don't open the squared brackets yet, because they might cancel. And they do. a minus b and b minus a are opposites, and opposites have the same square. And a and b are different, so that square is not zero. So the squared parts cancel.

We're left with b times a cubed, over a times b cubed. One a cancels from a cubed, which leaves a squared on top. One b cancels from b cubed, which leaves b squared at the bottom. So the answer is a squared over b squared. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way is to read the definition before calculating. The top and the bottom use the same two numbers, just swapped. The squared part is x minus y. Swapping x and y gives the opposite number inside, but the square is the same. So both fractions have the same top. When we divide one fraction by another with the same nonzero top, that top cancels.
at: but the square is the same

slides.say: So only the two denominators matter. The first fraction has a times b cubed, where b, its second input, is cubed. The second has b times a cubed, where a is cubed. These are not always equal, so they don't cancel. When we divide by the second fraction, its denominator, b a cubed, goes to the top. So we get b a cubed over a b cubed. One a and one b cancel, and we get a squared over b squared. Choice number three.
at: so we get b a cubed
a squared over b squared. Choice

slides.say: [pause] And plugging in numbers. a and b must be different, and neither can be zero. So let's take a is one and b is two. First, check that the choices come out different. One, one half, one quarter and four. All different, so one plug-in is enough.

The top is diamond of one and two. One minus two is negative one, and squared that's one. Below it, one times two cubed is eight. So the top is one eighth. The bottom is diamond of two and one. Two minus one is one, squared one. Below it, two times one cubed is two. So the bottom is one half.
at: The top is diamond of one and two

slides.say: One eighth divided by one half is one eighth times two, which is one quarter. That's choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
